design.sampling: every 6 simulated minutes: minute, maxGen, population, bodied, eyed bodied
design.execution: four browser tabs in parallel, one arm each; terrain guard, fixed geometry, preflight resize and fingerprint tests passed in every tab before any run

primary.test: s(eye | 1 part) in th0_eye1 above +10 percent with 95 percent interval above zero
primary.verdict: FAILED, and the interval lies entirely below zero: wired to food, the eye is selected against.
primary.falsifierTriggered: If s(eye | 1 part) is not above zero in the (0,1) arm, the wiring was not the problem, and under the v1.42 falsifier the vision line is set aside in favour of the body cost.

reportedNotSubstituted.note: With bodies cheaper to breed the food wired eye turns mildly positive, +4.6 percent with an interval of +1.3 to +7.9. Short of the +10 percent bar, and not a substitute for the primary test.

controls.note: Eye not wired to food: indistinguishable from zero in both, reproducing v1.42's -2.4 percent.

secondary.test: eyed share among bodied creatures above 50 percent for 100 generations, bodied >= 10, in >= 4 of 6 seeds

threshold.pilot: The two seed pilot put the fraction removed at 43 percent; six seeds put it at 35 (eye not wired) and 39 (eye wired).

exploratory_notPreregistered.note: At two parts the sign flips in both eye arms: +35.4 percent where one part was -11.7, and -14.0 where one part was +4.6. Several eye comparisons were examined, samples at two parts are small, and signs that flip with context are what a lineage confound would produce.

interpretation: The preregistered test failed decisively. Seeing food farther away did not make an eye pay; it made it cost.

Two candidate explanations cannot be told apart by this design. First, a mechanism in the code: a creature with food in sight heads for it at full speed (arrive rises with distance, index.html:1343) while one with no target wanders at 75 percent speed (index.html:1483), and movement burn grows with speed squared (index.html:1500). An eye that finds distant food in a grazed, crowded dish may mostly buy expensive chases lost to nearer grazers. Second, a design limit: eyed and eyeless creatures are not randomised, so the effect of an eye cannot be separated from the lineage that happens to carry it, and small, context dependent, sign flipping effects are its signature.

A randomised common garden design would separate them: release matched genomes that differ only in an eye into the same world and compare their descendants. The Workshop already releases designed genomes deterministically.
The breeding threshold is a real, large share of the body cost, about a third of it, not the majority the hypothesis proposed.

reproducibility.asPreregistered: FAILED: the control arm did not reproduce the v1.42 ledger exactly.
reproducibility.cause: The v1.43 harness checked the generation 400 stop every 60 steps; the v1.42 harness every 3,600. Runs stopped slightly earlier and recorded fewer deaths.
reproducibility.verification: Seed 60606 rerun on v1.43 with the stop checked every 3,600 steps reproduced the v1.42 ledger in every field (n, offspring, lifespan, algae, flesh, eyeSum, parts): 67,490 individuals, zero differences. The 60 step rule stopped at step 1,123,080 and the 3,600 step rule at 1,123,200.
consequences: v1.43 with both switches off is bit for bit v1.42 at WORLD 3 over 400 generations.
The stop rule is identical across all four arms, so between arm comparisons are unaffected.
The v1.42 eye selection study was not perturbed by the resize hazard found during this run.

toolingFaults: The game's window resize handler regenerates terrain and rescues creatures, drawing from the simulation's random stream; a capture phase event block failed its own test because the game's listener fires first. Fixed by guarding genTerrain and rescue so only initWorld may call them during a study.

The desktop app clears emulated viewports when a turn ends; the game recomputed R in three tabs (to 822 and 1074), the harness's geometry guard stopped them, and three runs were voided and rerun. Fixed by fixing study geometry at 1280x720 regardless of the window.
Stop check granularity differed from the previous study (see reproducibility).
zsh does not word split an unquoted variable, so the first progress monitor read no logs and reported only a stall. Replaced with a Python watcher.
honestLimitations: Observational: eyes are whatever mutation produced, not randomised.
One machine; cross machine determinism is known broken.
Six seeds per arm, 400 generations each.
EYE_FOOD's wider algae query is also the neighbourhood the mouth scans, part of the switch rather than a separate effect.
